title: Floral spring simmer pot
subtitle: A hob simmer with rose petals, jasmine, lemon, and mint
excerpt: Floral spring simmer pot is a pan of water simmered on the hob with dried rose petals, dried jasmine flowers, a strip of lemon peel, and fresh mint, releasing a light, clean floral scent around the kitchen. The simmer fills a large kitchen with scent in about ten minutes and keeps going for two to three hours on low heat with occasional top-ups. Use once and discard the botanicals.
sourceNotes: Simmer pot tradition documented in Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management (1861) and Natural Home by Janet Sawyer (2014). The combination of floral botanicals (rose, jasmine) with a citrus note (lemon peel) and a herbal freshness (mint) follows classical pot-pourri composition principles.

recipe.batchNotes: Prepare a fresh simmer pot per session. The botanicals are single-use.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep a small jar of the dry botanical blend ready to use. Add the lemon peel and fresh mint at simmer time.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Single use only. Discard the botanicals after the simmer session.

content.text: Floral spring simmer pot is a pan of water simmered on the hob with dried rose petals, dried jasmine flowers, a strip of fresh lemon peel, and a few sprigs of mint, releasing a light, clean floral scent around the kitchen. The simmer fills a large kitchen with scent in about ten minutes and keeps going for two to three hours on low heat with occasional water top-ups. Use once and discard the botanicals.

items.prepNote: dried rose petals from a pot-pourri supplier or dried from the garden
dried jasmine flowers; substitute fresh if available
fresh lemon peel, pared wide with a vegetable peeler; no white pith if possible
substitute fresh mint if available; adds a herby freshness to offset the florals
enough to simmer for 2 to 3 hours; top up as needed

content.text: Combine all the botanicals with the water in a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Reduce to low and leave to simmer, uncovered, for as long as needed. The scent develops fully within ten minutes. Top up with more water as the level drops, do not let the pan run dry. Never leave the hob unattended with the simmer pot on.

For a stronger floral throw, add a few drops of rose or jasmine essential oil to the water. For a simpler version without dried flowers, a strip of lemon peel, a sprig of fresh rosemary, and a few lavender stalks gives a bright, herby kitchen scent.
Discard the spent botanicals after the simmer session. They are compostable. Rinse the pan, the coloured liquid stains if left to dry.
